subject.title: RFC: Org claim disputes and account recovery

question: Should the current namespace-claim documentation/form and account-recovery tooling be accepted as the final policy outcome for this RFC, or should this RFC stay open until a separate accepted policy/runbook is written?
rationale: Current main implements intake and recovery mechanics, but the RFC itself is still Draft with open policy questions and the item is collaborator-authored with security/product-review labels, so automation cannot decide acceptance.

options.title: Keep RFC open for synthesis
options.body: Use the existing docs/form/recovery endpoints as inputs and keep the RFC open until maintainers publish accepted public policy plus any private reviewer runbook.

options.title: Accept current implementation
options.body: Declare the current namespace-claim docs/form and account-recovery tooling sufficient, then close only after a maintainer-owned policy note links the evidence.

recommendation.title: Keep RFC open for synthesis
recommendation.body: Use the existing docs/form/recovery endpoints as inputs and keep the RFC open until maintainers publish accepted public policy plus any private reviewer runbook.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the RFC and related namespace-claim implementation, making them the clearest owner for the acceptance/synthesis decision.
